credential: Free IBM SkillsBuild Artificial Intelligence Fundamentals digital credential
scope_notes: Approximately ten-hour IBM SkillsBuild learning plan covering AI history and applications, prediction, natural-language processing, computer vision, machine learning, deep learning, neural networks and AI ethics, with a hands-on machine-learning model simulation and credential assessment.
prerequisites: No formal technical prerequisite verified; designed as an intermediate/foundational AI career-entry pathway
required_resources: Modern browser and free IBM SkillsBuild account; practice simulations and Watson Studio-oriented activities are delivered through the SkillsBuild learning environment

component_evidence.pedagogy: The prescribed learning plan progresses from AI concepts and applications into language, vision, machine learning, neural networks and ethics, finishing with career context and practical model-oriented simulation rather than relying on passive reading alone.
component_evidence.depth: The plan provides a broad AI survey over roughly ten hours, enough for meaningful conceptual grounding but far less mathematical, programming and project depth than CS50 AI or a dedicated machine-learning course.
component_evidence.practice: IBM requires graded quizzes, final assessments and practice simulations for the credential, and the course includes a hands-on simulation in which learners build and test a machine-learning model. Practice is real but bounded compared with project-heavy incumbents.
component_evidence.materials: IBM SkillsBuild supplies a structured multi-course plan, interactive learning activities, assessments, simulations and a digital credential; public granular lesson materials are less transparent than fully open university-course packages.
component_evidence.currency: The credential and learner route are current in the 2026 SkillsBuild catalog. Core AI concepts remain relevant, but the pathway's centre of gravity is classical AI/Watson Studio rather than the newest generative-AI and agentic workflows, so currency is strong rather than category-leading.
component_evidence.expertise: IBM has direct expertise in enterprise AI, Watson/watsonx, machine learning and workforce training, and the credential is designed and issued by IBM SkillsBuild.
component_evidence.accessibility: The course and credential are free, self-paced and browser-based with low financial friction. A registered SkillsBuild account is required, but there is no verified mandatory paid software or hardware.

recommendation_rationale: A strong free broad AI-literacy/fundamentals credential with real assessment and simulation, especially for learners who value low-friction structure and recognition. It is not the strongest canonical AI foundation: Google ML Crash Course is substantially more current and interactive for ML, Kaggle is more practice-dense for beginner modelling, and CS50 AI is much deeper and project-heavy.

credential: Free IBM SkillsBuild Data Fundamentals digital credential
scope_notes: Seven-hour IBM SkillsBuild data foundation covering data analytics concepts, data-science methodologies, the data ecosystem, cleaning, refining and visualising data with IBM Watson Studio, with graded quizzes, final assessments and practice simulations.
prerequisites: No formal prerequisite verified; intended as an intermediate/foundational data pathway for registered learners
required_resources: Modern browser and free IBM SkillsBuild account; practice simulations and Watson Studio-oriented activities are provided through the learning environment

component_evidence.pedagogy: The pathway moves from data concepts and analytics methodology into practical cleaning, refinement and visualisation, connecting conceptual data-science workflow with tool-based simulations.
component_evidence.depth: Seven hours provide a credible foundation but cannot match the breadth of a 30-hour analytics curriculum spanning spreadsheets, SQL, visualisation and portfolio work.
component_evidence.practice: Credential criteria require graded quizzes, final assessments and practice simulations, including cleaning, refining and visualising data. The practice layer is substantial for the duration but narrower than Cisco's lab-heavy analytics route.
component_evidence.materials: IBM provides a structured learning plan, simulations, assessments and credentialing. Public lesson-level transparency is more limited than open-courseware packages, and the tool context centres on IBM Watson Studio.
component_evidence.currency: The course is current in the 2026 SkillsBuild catalog and the data-workflow fundamentals remain useful, but Watson Studio-specific examples and the compact scope create more maintenance risk than tool-neutral statistical/data foundations.
component_evidence.expertise: IBM has strong professional expertise in data platforms, analytics, AI and workforce education, giving the course credible applied framing.
component_evidence.accessibility: The seven-hour route and credential are free, self-paced and available to registered learners. No mandatory paid software or physical equipment is verified.

recommendation_rationale: A useful compact data foundation with a genuine free credential and practice simulations. Cisco Data Analytics Essentials remains the stronger core recommendation because its roughly 30-hour route adds spreadsheets, SQL, Tableau, more than twenty labs, module/final exams and portfolio work; IBM is better treated as a concise alternative rather than another canonical analytics slot.
